bank: EYES E18 [he can hear it] -- the axis card spec, round one of two
note: SCHOOL ROUND. Nothing here is a measurement and nothing here is in the game. This is the spec round two builds, with every decision traced to the finding that forced it.

the_anchor.track: BESAID ISLAND, FINAL FANTASY X Original Soundtrack, disc 1 track 18
the_anchor.which_version: THE ORIGINAL, not the HD Remaster, his words

the_candidate.name: THE MARKER ON THE DOOR
the_candidate.his_words: The marker on the door at full intensity is now one of my new favorite songs that you've made great job
the_candidate.where_it_lives: the alpha and the demo. NOT in the walked city file, which is the permanently-NIGHT music gap the laws master already carries.

axes.ours: 120 BPM, fixed by the 120 BPM LAW
axes.reference: UNKNOWN. every public number is for a cover
axes.why: counter-finding (c): changing our tempo breaks a pillar law, so a gap here is not a defect

axes.ours: first percussive onset in seconds, off a real render
axes.reference: CITED TEXT, from a source, no invented number
axes.why: the axis he actually responded to, and an onset time needs no beat tracker

axes.ours: step pattern and named voice, presence and register off the render
axes.why: a played bass line and a step pattern are comparable as floor-holding, not as performance

axes.ours: pentatonic contour off the row, Parsons code plus DTW
axes.why: Parsons showed interval direction alone separates a large number of tunes; DTW handles two different speeds

axes.ours: a sawtooth through a synth voice
axes.reference: real violin, hand percussion, picked strings
axes.why: counter-finding (e): a synth patch and a violin are not two points on one ruler. what CAN be checked is the ROLE each voice plays: lead carries the tune, bass holds the floor, pad holds the room.

banned_by_school: a similarity score, a percentage, or a ranking of 200 songs by distance from Besaid. Temp love outside, and our own 8/27 batch-25 post-mortem inside, both say a distance metric walks away from his taste.

any BPM or key lifted off a BPM database. Those entries are covers by Celestial Aeon Project, Franco Albertini, Josh Barron, Jeremy Ng, Game Soundtrack Cat and PianoDreams, spread from about 103 to 175 BPM, E major on one and C#/Db minor on another.
inheriting our own law's original-versus-remaster description, which points the opposite way to every source reachable this round.
reaching for the standard reference-comparison plugin. Metric AB and Reference 2 measure loudness, spectrum, stereo image, correlation and dynamics: production, not one of the five axes.
controls: RENDER: the song must come back as sound, not silence. Reuse E12's tap.

OCTAVE ERROR: a click train at a known 120 reads 120, and the same train at half speed reads 60 and NOT 120. Mandatory, because the standard DBN's 55 BPM floor forces double-tempo on slow music and percussion presence changes performance.
CONTOUR: a melody against itself reads identical, against its own inversion reads maximally different.
BEAT ENTRY: a planted onset at a known time is found at that time.
all controls pass or no number is printed.
reuse_not_rebuild: tools/bohemia_sfx_instrument_measure.py already reaches the live 602-voice rack in the one alpha
tools/bohemia_eyes_quiet.js already taps the audio graph and does BS.1770 loudness
loudness is matched before any A/B, which is the one thing the standard tool gets right
no_ratchet: Nothing here can only get worse, so nothing is frozen. What can go stale is a reference-side value with no source behind it, so any gate from round two holds that every reference value carries its own source string and is verified present, the shape PRE-JUDGE COVERAGE already uses.
what_this_lane_may_not_do: decide whether the song is good. That is DIRECTION and SOUNDS. This lane reports numbers and says which side each one is from.
